title: Assumption method
examples: Can you show me how to use this method with money?
Is this method always the best way to solve word problems?
What if I have more than two types of objects?

explain.say: Today we learn a helpful thinking method. It is called the assumption method. We use this when a problem seems tricky.
First, we make a simple guess about the problem. We assume a number for one part of the problem. This is our first assumption.
Next, we use that assumption to calculate the rest of the problem. We check if our numbers match what the problem says. This is the checking step.
If the numbers do not match, we adjust our first guess. We change the assumption a little bit and try again. This is the adjustment step.
For example, suppose you have chickens and rabbits. You might assume all animals are chickens first. Then you adjust to include rabbits.

faq.q: What if I get the right answer on my first guess?
faq.a: That is great! You do not need to adjust anything. Your first assumption was correct for that problem.
asks: Do I stop guessing if it works?
What if the first guess is perfect?

faq.q: Can I use this method for anything, or only animals?
faq.a: You can use it for many types of problems, not just animals. It helps with finding unknown numbers in word problems.
asks: Does this only work for coins?
Is this only for counting things?

faq.q: When should I use this method instead of equations?
faq.a: Use this when setting up equations seems too hard or confusing. It is a good stepping stone to understanding the math.
asks: When is this better than writing an equation?

faq.q: How do I know how much to adjust my guess?
faq.a: Look at the difference between what you got and what the problem needs. Adjust your guess by that difference.
asks: How big should my next guess be?
What is the rule for adjusting?

faq.q: Does this method always give the answer?
faq.a: It helps you find the answer by testing possibilities. Sometimes, you might need to try a few times to find the correct one.
asks: Will I always find the answer this way?

facts: The assumption method is a problem-solving strategy.
It involves making an initial guess about the unknown values.
After guessing, you must check your guess against the problem details.
If the check fails, you adjust your initial guess systematically.

quiz.say: If you assume all items are Type A, and the total count is too high, what should you do next?
quiz.why: If your total is too high, it means you guessed too much of the Type A items, so you must decrease that guess.

wrong.0: If the total is wrong, keeping the assumption the same will never fix the problem.
wrong.1: While adjusting, dividing by two is not the correct systematic step based on the error.
wrong.3: This makes the total even higher, moving you further from the correct answer.

quiz.say: You are counting items and your first guess is too low. What adjustment should you make?
quiz.why: If your total is too low, it means you guessed too little of the item, so you must increase that guess.

wrong.0: Decreasing the guess when the total is already low will make the answer even smaller.
wrong.1: If the total is wrong, keeping the assumption the same will not help you find the correct number.
wrong.2: There is no rule to multiply by three; you must adjust based on the error.

quiz.say: When using this method, what is the most important step after making a guess?
quiz.show: Check the guess against the problem

options.show: Check the guess against the problem
options.say: Check the guess against the problem

quiz.why: You must always check your initial guess against the problem's rules to see if it is correct or if adjustment is needed.

wrong.0: You cannot adjust without first knowing if the original guess was wrong.
wrong.1: While equations help, the assumption method focuses first on testing numbers, not setting up symbols.
wrong.2: This is not a mathematical step; you must use your own checking skills first.
